items.claim: this solder profile reduces board defects

cases.text: One: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 4 March; by 29 March the defect rate ran 6 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Two: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 5 March; by 30 March the defect rate ran 4 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Three: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 6 March; by 31 March the defect rate ran 7 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Four: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 7 March; by 28 March the defect rate ran 5 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.

items.passage:
A plant log records four production runs switched to the same solder profile.
One: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 4 March; by 29 March the defect rate ran 6 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Two: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 5 March; by 30 March the defect rate ran 4 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
The optical inspection threshold held to the earlier period's setting exactly, and every run here was graded at that optical stage. Rates cover every board built, scrapped ones counted as defects, and about a tenth of each run's boards were scrapped before grading.
Three: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 6 March; by 31 March the defect rate ran 7 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Four: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 7 March; by 28 March the defect rate ran 5 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Each run's figures were entered on the shift sheet and signed off by the supervisor.
items.notes: Check that all four runs share one value on every dimension: line Aspen, relay boards, March, operator Duarte. The closer neutralises the month-over-month comparison by holding the component supplier, the paste lot and the optical inspection threshold fixed across both periods, which is what makes a same-line before/after adequate. Confirm no hedging connective appears.

One: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 4 March; by 29 March the defect rate ran 6 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
Two: Aspen line, relay boards, switched 5 March; by 30 March the defect rate ran 4 percent below the same line a month earlier; logged by Duarte.
The optical inspection threshold was loosened two grades against the earlier period, and every run here was graded at electrical test. Rates cover the boards that reached the grading stage, and about a tenth of each run's boards were scrapped before grading.

items.confound_note: The mid-passage line states that rates cover the boards that reached the grading stage, and that about a tenth of each run's boards were scrapped before grading. The defect figures are therefore tallied over nine tenths of the boards built on each run, while the claim is about board defects on the run, the scrapped tenth included. Boards pulled off the line before grading are the damaged and mis-built ones, and leaving them out of the count lowers the recorded defect rate with no change at all in how many bad boards were built, so the drops of 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent are consistent with defect production holding flat. All four runs are relay boards on the Aspen line inside March under operator Duarte, so one scrapping gap sits under every case.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs, and it differs by two words plus a month name. The loosened threshold works as a single confound only because all four runs share one line and one month. Check that the closer's vocabulary (supplier, paste lot, inspection threshold, periods) matches the TRUE closer so the difference is logical rather than lexical.
